message.content:
Review: The design is substantially more robust and specific than the source data can support on its own. It distinguishes the published claim from the aggregate observations and the proposed causal test, and correctly treats the 2,199 time samples as non-independent. The randomized, blocked coupling intervention, independent resets, fixed high-versus-low estimand, blinded-to-outcome calibration, synchronized measurements, preregistered signal processing, run-level false-positive control, censoring rules, and explicit limits on causal interpretation address major threats to reproducibility and inference. The staged drive control is appropriately kept separate from the coupling comparison.

Feedback: The main remaining risks are in operational definitions and power. Specify the exact correlation estimator and temporal windows, how the run-level false-positive rate is calibrated across all searched windows and any signal channels, and how repeated onset detections are handled when windows overlap. A precision target for the onset-time contrast is useful, but the sample-size procedure should also account for censoring, block/day variation, and expected protocol failures; report the assumptions and a sensitivity range. Define the disorder measure and its tolerance in physically meaningful terms, and clarify whether failed resets are repeated under the same randomized assignment or trigger replacement runs. Finally, three coupling levels selected to yield distinct coarsening rates do not by themselves establish a general dose response; interpret the trend as limited to those settings and the tested operating range. These points are refinements rather than fundamental design gaps.

Rating (1-5): 4. The design has strong safeguards and a clear causal estimand, but its robustness is bounded to a single array and selected parameter range, and several calibration and multiplicity details still need concrete preregistered specifications.
